newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian dollar opens stronger, eyes U.S. numbers.
newsitem.headline: Canadian dollar opens stronger, eyes U.S. numbers.

text.p: * The Canadian dollar opened firmer after posting gains on Tuesday following unexpectedly muted U.S. economic data which quelled inflation and interest rate fears. * The currency opened at C$1.3960 (US$0.7163) versus a close of C$1.3975 (US$0.7156). * Investors will keep a keen eye on U.S. numbers due out this week, particularly Friday's nonfarm payrolls.

Canadian and U.S. financial markets rallied on Tuesday after news that U.S. durable goods orders fell more than expected in March, while the U.S. employment cost index for the first quarter rose less than expected.
On Wednesday, Statistics Canada announced that Canada's real gross domestic product rose 0.5 percent in February over the month before.
The U.S. gross domestic product rose an unexpectedly large 5.6 percent in the first quarter while the price index climbed 2.7 percent.
The implicit price deflator gained 2.3 percent.

Farrill said financial markets will be chiefly concerned with Friday's avidly watched nonfarm payrolls numbers. Nonfarm payrolls were seen rising 211,000 in April while the unemployment rate was seen unchanged at 5.2 percent.
On the crosses, the Canadian dollar firmed to 1.2383 marks from 1.2339 on Tuesday. Against the yen, the unit was slightly weaker at 90.76 yen versus 90.79 yen.
((Sarah Edmonds, Reuters Toronto Bureau (416) 941-8100, E-mail sarah.edmonds@reuters.com))
